clue.text: Flights from London in planes appear dubious for vacation, unfortunately

definitions.note: a Londoner's Cockney rhyming slang for stairs, which come in flights

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is a bad one, so these letters are jumbled into a new order
vacating a word empties it of its insides, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A traveller fears that planes look unreliable for a holiday trip out of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for vacation' empties DUBIOUS to DS; 'unfortunately' scrambles PLANES APPEAR plus DS. 'Apples and pears' is Cockney rhyming slang (London street slang where a rhyming phrase stands for a word) for stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairs come in flights, and London's Cockney slang calls stairs apples and pears, rhyming with the word it replaces.

clue.text: Athletics event in European cellar

parts.note: a Pole is a European, a native of Poland
a vault is an underground cellar or storeroom

explanation.surface: Someone stages a track-and-field contest in a basement somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is a field event in which competitors clear a high bar using a flexible pole.

clue.text: Film actor taking top off

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: an actor is a player on the stage

explanation.surface: A movie star strips off their shirt, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a cinema word, but here it means a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a thin coating spread over a surface, which is one layer.

clue.text: She can broadcast about idiot Englishman

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, i.e. around, the other piece
seeds broadcast are scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A woman talks on air about some foolish Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles SHE CAN into SENACH, and 'about' puts it around ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scottish, often disparaging, term for an English person.

clue.text: Hot drink, say, absorbed by revolutionary rag

indicators.note: one piece is taken into the other, ending up inside it
a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a downmarket newspaper, such as the Sun, a British tabloid
eg, for example, is what 'say' means when it introduces an instance

explanation.surface: A hot drink is soaked up by a radical newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' is slang for a low-grade newspaper; the Sun is a British tabloid. 'say' looks like speech but stands for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is an old hot drink of port or sherry mixed with sugar, spice and hot water.

clue.text: Gay parent's elaborate display

indicators.note: something elaborate is intricately worked, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheerful mother or father puts on a showy exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' does double duty: it scrambles GAY PARENT and also belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is splendid ceremonial show, a lavish public spectacle.

clue.text: Cut off a bit

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece of something

explanation.surface: Someone slices off a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off from others means being separated, set at a distance from them.

clue.text: Easy when half-cut, checks for groups with attractive bodies

indicators.note: half-cut usually means drunk, but here the word loses half its letters, keeping the back half

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check or stop it

explanation.surface: A tipsy partygoer goes looking for clubs full of good-looking people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves EASY to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetary or star systems are groups of bodies held together by mutual gravitational attraction.

clue.text: Decide not to be involved in work with dodgy ticket seller

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to do business with a shady scalper.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout is the British word for a ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part in a scheme or arrangement.

clue.text: Prince and friend getting close

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A royal and his companion are becoming intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pally is informal for friendly, the way close friends are.

clue.text: Southern leader excited by Arkansas being oddly deficient in forage for cattle

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: agog means eager and excited

indicators.note: lacking the odd-numbered letters, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A southern politician is thrilled by a state that somehow lacks animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly deficient' strips the odd letters from ARKANSAS, leaving RASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago grass is an Australian pasture grass grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Watch Victor swapping places with son? The opposite

indicators.note: swapping signals an exchange, so the second letter goes back where the first one was
one letter takes the place of the other in the word, half of the swap

parts.note: to watch is to observe
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
Victor is V in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A man asks whether his watch has been switched round with his boy's, ending up the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping places with' exchanges the V and the S in OBSERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the counterpart or opposite of a statement, and also the face side of a coin.

clue.text: Work out around American city

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to work out a dispute is to settle it

explanation.surface: Someone exercises near a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' suggests the gym, but it means resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major city in Washington state in the US Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: One may be opposed to request

definitions.meaning: the opposable digit, able to be placed opposite the fingers
to ... a lift is to request a ride by hitchhiking

explanation.definitionFit: The thumb opposes the fingers in gripping, and hitchhikers ask for rides by thumbing.

clue.text: Bishop doing cow impressions excited to be going viral, perhaps

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
lowing is mooing, the sound a cow makes
up can mean excited or worked up

explanation.surface: A clergyman mooing like a cow gets worked up about becoming an internet sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blowing up online is suddenly becoming hugely popular, as when a post spreads rapidly.

clue.text: Scotland sorts out constant burden

parts.note: Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland

indicators.note: out here means not in order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Scotland deals with an ever-present problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles SORTS into TROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: An albatross round one's neck, from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, is a heavy, inescapable encumbrance.

clue.text: Hood in dodgy cabal getting hot material

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: lava is molten rock, hot material from a volcano

explanation.surface: A masked hoodlum in a shady clique gets hold of some stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' suggests a criminal, but here it is a head covering; 'dodgy' scrambles CABAL into BALAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A balaclava is a close-fitting knitted covering for the head and neck, leaving the face partly open.

clue.text: In a legitimate position to suppress article secretly

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second down inside it

parts.note: onside, in football, means legally positioned, not offside
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone with official standing gags a newspaper piece covertly.
explanation.walkthrough: Onside is a football term: a player not in an offside position.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the side means doing it covertly, apart from one's main activity.

clue.text: Promise to marry criminal at brothel

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong, so these letters are put wrongly in a new order

explanation.surface: An engagement is formed by a crook at a house of ill repute.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a formal engagement, a pledge that two people will wed.

clue.text: Rustic tramp nearly gets abdominal pain

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp
colic is severe pain in the abdomen

explanation.surface: A countryside vagrant nearly gets a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts BUM to BU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes country life, pastoral and rural.

clue.text: In spite of everything, I start to search for legendary creatures

parts.note: yet can mean nevertheless, in spite of everything

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to begin hunting for mythical beasts regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Yetis are mythical apelike beasts said to roam the Himalayas, also called abominable snowmen.

clue.text: Figure out former partner is somewhere in south England

parts.note: to suss something is to work it out
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Someone works out that their former partner lives in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a historic county on England's south coast; suss is British informal for work out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is a county on the English Channel coast, a region of southern England.

clue.text: Movement of car rested back of skull

indicators.note: movement of letters shifts them around into a new order
back here means the word is read backwards

parts.note: lain is the past participle of lie, so rested

explanation.surface: A moving car stopped and the rear of someone's head was hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement of' scrambles CAR into CRA, and 'back' turns LAIN into NIAL. 'back of skull' looks like the definition, but 'back' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranial is the adjective for the cranium, the bony case of the head.

clue.text: Snake occasionally seen in beer joint

indicators.note: one piece appears inside the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A serpent is now and then spotted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a pub or cut of meat, but here it is part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint linking the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Possibly Rice has penned this?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so these words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A question about what a famous wordsmith might have written.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Rice wrote the words for musicals such as Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Rice is a celebrated lyricist, so the words of a song are exactly what he writes.

clue.text: Extremely crafty journalists found in tree

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Very cunning reporters turn up in a woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a coniferous evergreen, often tall and slender.

clue.text: Ring contains rare gem

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
R is the abbreviation for rare, as for underdone steak

explanation.surface: A ring is set with an unusual jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery, but it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a lustrous concretion formed in an oyster, prized as a jewel.

clue.text: In Italy, a mere 50% of road rage takes place, essentially, with learner reversing

indicators.note: the whole string is read backwards to give the entry
half of the word is used, here its back half
the essence of a word is its central letter, taken from each word

parts.note: L is the learner symbol on plates for new drivers

explanation.surface: Only half the road-rage incidents happen in Italy, mostly with a learner driver backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' gives AD; 'essentially' gives K and A, the middles of TAKES and PLACE; 'reversing' turns ADRAGEKAL around. A mere is a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy, and a mere is a lake.

clue.text: Such seminal frames from the east

definitions.text: Such seminal frames from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east is reading right to left
the word frames, or surrounds, the answer within it

explanation.surface: Pioneering film stills from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' holds EMINA inside SEMINAL; 'from the east' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is Japanese animated film, drawn frame by frame and coming from the Far East.

clue.text: Acrylic sweeper agitated spiders, for example

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A synthetic broom disturbed some arachnids.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy-crawlies are small insects and spiders, especially ones people find unpleasant.
